newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Big Wall Street rally boosts European shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Big Wall Street rally boosts European shares.

text.p: Leading European stock markets were given a modest boost on Wednesday by a late burst of activity on Wall Street overnight, which helped the Dow score its second biggest one-day gain ever.
On the currency front the dollar edged lower against the mark and yen after profit-taking overnight knocked it back from Tuesday's 37-month high of 1.7375 marks.
British, German and French blue chips all took early comfort from the dramatic rise in U.S. stocks but fell back from their highs later in the morning amid cautious trading.

The Dow Jones industrial average had ended up 135.26 points at 6,587.16 after encouraging U.S. inflation data raised hopes that interest rates might not have to be raised as steeply as had been feared.
In London trading volumes were light as continuing economic and political uncertainties weighed on investor sentiment.
"As expected we have rallied on the back of Wall Street," one senior dealer said. "But people are sitting on their hands for the moment. No one wants to be too brave."

London shares were underpinned to a degree by British unemployment figures which, as expected, showed a 41,000 drop in the jobless total in March. But dealers said volumes were light as institutional investors stayed on the sidelines.

"We've had a bit of a mark-up but the fund managers still don't want to do too much," the head of trading at a major investment house said. "There is still too much uncertainty about for the market to go charging forward."

Fears that the opposition Labour Party, the clear favourite to win Britain's May 1 election, would need to raise corporate taxes to shore up fragile government finances were cited as a contributing factor to the FTSE index's recent thin trading volumes.
Analysts also cited worries that a Labour finance minister might agree to a 50 basis point interest rate rise shortly after the ballot in order to establish credibility with the financial markets.

In Frankfurt the DAX index of bourse floor trading was up 1.1 percent in early trade but by late morning had pared its gains and was three quarters of a percent up. Dealers said the market was being held back somewhat by the weaker dollar.

New result details from Daimler-Benz were viewed positively but not with the same enthusiasm that greeted recent figures from BMW. Upgrades were nonetheless expected to result from an analysts' meeting later in the day, dealers said.
Daimler's shares were trading at 138.2 marks by 1030 GMT after earlier reaching an all-time high of 142.40.
In Paris French shares also fell back from their peak of over half a percent up but were still in positive territory following the bourse's 2.12 percent gain on Tuesday.

Currency traders said Tuesday's surge in the Dow and U.S. Treasury markets failed to hold the dollar above 1.73 marks but it still looked well-supported and speculation on higher U.S. interest rates was still in place.
"The Dow and bonds surge was purely a domestic reaction to the soft CPI data and seemed a more technical correction of its recent falls," said a Japanese bank dealer.
Against the yen, the dollar orbited the 126 yen level in morning European business, down from overnight levels amid continuing concern about possible Bank of Japan intervention.

Comments overnight from senior Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara, who reiterated official concerns over excessive currency moves, further dampened the upside potential for the dollar/yen rate.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7250 marks and 126.03 yen after ending at 1.7333 and 126.28 in late trading in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 4.0 points at 4,290.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 7.12 points at 2,627.75.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 25.74 points at 3,353.13.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed lower at $341.45 versus $341.75 at the close in London on Tuesday. Silver was firmer at $4.73.
